steps.what: Listen and provide emotional support and encouragement to psychiatric patients

tasks.design: Keep the supportive conversation with the aide and patient. Care guidance in {DOCS} can support preparation, but this task establishes no separate administrative baseline to remove.
tasks.previous_blocker: Support depends on trust and response to the patient's present experience.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability establishes a safe time reduction for the human interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Distress may be difficult to express and may change during the interaction.
tasks.human_edge: Notice discomfort, listen without rushing and seek clinical help when needed.
tasks.altitude: Patient contact and the aide's clinical boundaries remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How to distinguish an observation from a clinical interpretation

evidence.claim: Direct emotional support remains interpersonal work; the digest's letter and dictation tools do not establish replacement of supportive psychiatric care.

assumptions: Boundary is the supportive interaction, excluding separate recording and clinical decision-making. No care minutes are relabelled as paperwork.

Clinical staff supply care guidance before the interaction. The patient supplies expressions during s1; understanding and clarification occur within its full time, without a free distress or suitability flag.
Native guidance access is considered before code. No new service or transferred work is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Current care guidance and escalation responsibilities
research_questions: What information do aides need from clinical staff before supporting a distressed patient?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Supportive contact has no supported time reduction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Complete physical checks and monitor patients for unusual or harmful behavior
Report observations and clarify concerns with professional staff

tasks.design: Retain direct checks and prompt communication with professional staff. {DOCS} may hold existing instructions, but no new automated behavior interpretation or reporting queue replaces contact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meaningful changes require observation and context rather than a complete structured feed.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability removes physical checks or clarification under this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Urgency and incomplete observations require direct clinical communication.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize concerning changes and report precise observations without overstating a diagnosis.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring and escalation responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.task: Report a change in patient condition
reach.learn: What clinicians need to assess an observation promptly

evidence.claim: Direct checks and professional clarification cannot be treated as saved paperwork without a demonstrated change to those actions.

assumptions: Boundary includes checks and immediate reporting; durable record maintenance belongs to 18697 and is counted once. Professional staff's subsequent assessment stays outside this focal denominator unchanged.

Clinical staff provide current instructions before s1. The aide produces observations in s1; staff produce responses during s2 before clarification is completed. No structured harmful-behavior or urgency flag is assumed.
Consider existing care tools before custom code if a separate recording problem is evidenced. No new system means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Required observation intervals and communication channels
research_questions: Where do delays occur between an aide noticing a change and reaching clinical staff?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Physical checks and immediate clinical reporting retain their full shares.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work with the psychiatric care team

steps.what: Coordinate patient care observations and responsibilities with psychiatrists, psychologists, psychiatric nurses, or social workers

tasks.design: Keep multidisciplinary coordination with the people delivering care. Existing {DOCS} records support discussion without a new summary service or a claimed reduction in team contact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Team members must reconcile observations and understand responsibility in context.
tasks.enabler_now: No administrative substep with a supported reduction is established by this task.
tasks.still_hard: Different observations and changing care needs require clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Raise relevant observations, understand instructions and recognize the limits of the aide's role.
tasks.altitude: Team participation and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How activity plans relate to the multidisciplinary care plan

evidence.claim: Multidisciplinary care coordination remains an interpersonal task; no separate preparation or minutes baseline is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is aide participation in coordination, excluding original observation, record entry and other professionals' clinical decisions. Overlap with 18696 is assigned to immediate reporting there, not saved twice.
Team members bring observations and decisions to the discussion and clarify them during s1 before the aide confirms responsibilities. No free structured agreed-care or risk flag is assumed.
Native record access precedes custom code. No new tool, transferred work or recurring maintenance is proposed; upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How handover and multidisciplinary review are organized
research_questions: Which aide responsibilities remain unclear after current team discussions?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and net=0 with zero upkeep. No invented meeting preparation or minutes share is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify patient identity, observations and source instructions for the record
Record the aide's account in the electronic patient record
Check and commit the patient information entry

tasks.design: Test approved dictation inside {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, for the aide's own narrative. The aide supplies the account, corrects transcription and commits the exact entry; no clinical conclusions or treatment instructions are generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Typing a known account can duplicate the effort of composing it.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured speech entry can shorten typing while retaining author review.
tasks.still_hard: Negation, names, numbers and attribution must survive transcription correctly.
tasks.human_edge: Separate observation from inference and ensure the note accurately represents what happened.
tasks.altitude: Less typing if dictation fits the setting; recording responsibility is unchanged.

reach.task: Check the accuracy of dictated care documentation
reach.learn: How to detect omissions, negation errors and ambiguous attribution

evidence.claim: Microsoft Word Dictate supports spoken document entry, including Dutch preview support with an accuracy warning; this supports dictation capability, not compatibility with the local patient record.
The proposed patient record workflow and time savings are a conditional, unmeasured local scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is record maintenance, excluding original checks in 18696, emotional support and clinical authorship of treatment or discharge plans. The aide records only within delegated scope; other professionals' decisions remain unchanged.

Clinical staff produce treatment or discharge instructions before s1. In s1 the aide verifies patient ID, observation time, source author, measured value and unit where relevant, and exact instruction version. In s2 the aide personally dictates the account and corrects it within the retained 27 hours. No structured observation feed or inferred clinical flag is assumed; unsupported fields and uncertain transcription use manual entry.

OTHER means the electronic patient record. Test its native approved dictation before integration; use no external document service unless health-data access is approved. Existing speech entry earns no new saving.
unknowns: Whether approved dictation exists in the patient record
Whether quiet, private dictation is practical
research_questions: Does observed entry time fall after accounting for dictation corrections and patient identity checks?

already_counted.description: Meaning check and exact entry commitment

incremental.description: Dictation exception handling and vocabulary upkeep
Approved speech configuration and access support

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient ID, observation time, author attribution, values, units and narrative text committed by the aide; any edit requires renewed acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=35+45*0.6+20=82; gross=18, focal upkeep=5, central net=13. Range 0-5 allows short entries, noise, privacy constraints and transcription correction to consume most typing savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Care contact, observation and team coordination retain their time; approved dictation may reduce patient note typing.
reach: Learn documentation accuracy checks with a medical transcriptionist
role.ambitious_version: An aide who protects patient contact time while maintaining precise records within delegated clinical boundaries.
